current_answer: Google’s published Scale rule excludes startups that have received more than USD 5,000 in Google Cloud credits. Taking the Start tier’s up-to-USD 2,000 credit therefore does not, by that rule alone, bar a later Scale application. Scale still requires qualifying venture funding, company and round-age limits, evidence, and Google’s approval; no automatic upgrade or future award is promised.

catalogue_card.question: Will Google’s USD 2,000 Start credit block Scale later?
catalogue_card.text: Google’s published Scale rule excludes startups with more than USD 5,000 in prior Google Cloud credits, so a Start award at its USD 2,000 maximum does not itself cross that line. Scale still needs qualifying VC funding, round timing, and approval; there is no promised upgrade.

summary: Start offers up to USD 2,000 in Google Cloud credits for one year to eligible pre-funded startups.
Scale’s prior-credit gate is more than USD 5,000; Start at its published maximum is below it.
Scale still needs qualifying venture funding, company and round-age checks, funding proof, and discretionary approval.
Scale’s second year covers 20% of eligible usage up to an additional USD 100,000, not a second immediate cash balance.
Interledger applications remain paused; NLnet’s current form still lists 3 November 2026, 12:00 CET.
uncertainty: Google does not publish an automatic Start-to-Scale upgrade process or guarantee that prior Start participants will receive Scale credits; ask Google about the applicant-specific transition.
Google’s Scale page does not establish country-by-country coverage or an applicant-specific credit allocation.
Interledger Local Impact applications remain paused with no published reopening date; NLnet’s revised GenAI policy remains unpublished.
Microsoft and Cloudflare issuer-term conflicts remain unresolved. Pool analytics are unavailable.
